review.method: Acceptance suite run locally with `retail,gpu` (CS_GAME_DIR, CS_CAPABILITIES): the two ignored tests ran — the retail test read the installation's own ASSETS/LAYOUT.CSV MainMenu section and MAINMENU.SCRIPT into the shell, decoded the real CrimFlag.MPG through the production MpegVideoSource (320x240 @30.00 fps, its first frame's pixels non-uniform) and wrote front-end-mainmenu.json (the MM_LOGO/BFRAME panes, the `MOVIE` row's fields verbatim, the six MM_B_* buttons' `ResID=0` and stated effects), and the windowed test drove `cs --cs-path $CS_GAME_DIR --front-end --smoke-seconds 14 --capture-dir private/evidence/FE-MENU-2` on this machine's GPU (Apple M3 Pro, Metal), which wrote 11 real framebuffer PNGs and report.json: the flag movie opened and delivered 302 decoded frames to its texture under the panes at the row's 250%x250% (the authored 800x600), the pointer walk visited MainMenu → Campaign → MainMenu → InstantAction → MainMenu → Preferences (left by Esc, its return button's handler guarded) → MainMenu → Credits → MainMenu, the Multiplayer press was the one recorded unhandled press (`MultiPlayerMain` is no section), five Down presses walked the declaration order to Quit and Enter drove its `terminate`. Those records are the product's own output, hashed here; the assertions above are the acceptance run's own results. The run is scripted, never `human_play`, and no original executable ran. This harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, the MainMenu record, the smoke's report and the hashes of those artifacts. LIMITS: the original focus order, the loop's exact restart timing, the ResID label's string table and draw, the movie's own audio (FE-MENU-4's work), the movie Z-order beyond declaration order and which member the original maps onto the pointer are recorded unknowns in the shell's module docs and the smoke's report. Validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass.
